claims.text: This is an UPFRONT_QUOTE fare: quoted_fare_sgd is 13.00 and total_charged is 17.50 on the same artifact, an excess of 4.50. Under POL-RD-11 the distance and time charges on an upfront trip were fixed at booking — POL-RD-02 does not run — and the rider's remedy is the amount by which charged_total exceeds quoted_fare_sgd plus only the pass-through and statutory lines properly chargeable under POL-RD-09. The 13.00 quote itself stands, because the ride was taken; it is the 4.50 charged over it that is refundable in full.

Neither top-up that POL-RD-11(a) allows is present on this fare. The ERP and toll figure is 0.00 with an empty erp_gantries list, and the airport surcharge is 0.00 on a trip that neither originates nor ends at an airport, so a POL-RD-09 pass-through correction adds nothing to the 13.00 the rider agreed to. Nothing in the ledger accounts for the 4.50.

The rider does not ask the tribunal to find a route deviation, and on this trace none exists: the governing trace distance is 4.58 km against a 4.4 km optimal, an excess of 0.18 km and 4.09%, below both POL-RD-01 gates of 0.8 km and 20%. The claim is a billing claim. POL-RD-01 decides whether a deviation exists, not whether a fare that exceeds its own quote is refundable, and POL-RD-11 supplies the remedy for an upfront trip.

The driver does not defend the number. His statement on file says he keyed in another passenger's amount by mistake and would have corrected it had the rider spoken up. That is an admission that 17.50 does not price this trip — a 4.6 km, 14-minute ride from Bedok Mall to Parkway Parade — and it leaves the 4.50 excess over the 13.00 quote with no basis anywhere in the ledger.

The disputed money is still with the platform: payment_status is CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd is 0.00 on the fare. A refund of 4.50 out of the 17.50 charged returns part of the contested amount, which is a PARTIAL_REFUND under POL-GEN-03 and leaves the remainder of the charged fare standing.

No profile field decides this case, and the rider's own counters do not raise the bar. rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d and rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d_substantiated are both 0, so the POL-RD-08 corroboration requirement for a sub-30% excess is not engaged on this claim, whose excess is 4.09%. The driver's prior_deviation_flags is a lifetime counter, context only under POL-GEN-01, and is not the deviation_flags_90d that POL-RD-06 names.

claims.text: The establishment gate is not passed. The governing trace distance is 4.58 km against an optimal of 4.4 km (EV-GPS-00525 derived.deviation), an excess of only 0.18 km and 4.09 per cent. POL-RD-01 requires the excess to exceed both 0.8 km in absolute terms and 20 per cent of the optimal, and both tests must pass; here neither does. No deviation exists, and the outcome is NO_ACTION however the rider characterises the trip.

The rider carries the initial burden under POL-RD-08 and has not discharged it. She must show an excess meeting the POL-RD-01 threshold, measured from an unimpaired trace; the trace she relies on shows 0.18 km and 4.09 per cent. With no threshold-meeting excess, the claim fails for want of proof and no refund follows.

The trace is unimpaired for policy purposes: 85 fixes at a 10 second sample interval, 100 per cent coverage, no gaps and a maximum inter-fix gap of 0 seconds. None of POL-RD-07(a) to (c) fires, so no independent corroboration is required of anyone and no POL-RD-10(3) escalation arises.

There is no billing-integrity defect to refund under POL-RD-09(4). The fare_breakdown carries no off-route ERP or toll lines at all (0.00), no airport surcharge (the recorded pickup and dropoff labels are Bedok Mall and Parkway Parade, neither an airport, and the surcharge line is 0.00), and no waiting-time fee. No gantry is charged that the trace does not pass, so nothing is refundable as a standalone pass-through correction and POL-RD-10(8) is not engaged.

This is an UPFRONT_QUOTE trip (quoted_fare_sgd 13.00, non-null), so POL-RD-11 governs and POL-RD-02 does not run: the rider's distance and time were fixed at booking and no distance-or-time refund is available to her however large the excess. Her remedy on this fare model, if any, is confined to the arithmetic difference between charged_total and the quote - a billing-line question, not the route-deviation loss she pleads, and in no event the full amount contested.

No repeat-deviation pattern exists, so the POL-RD-06 remedy is unavailable to the rider: driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against driver_profile.completed_trips_90d of 250, far below both the '3 or more' and the '0.05 with at least 40 trips' tests. Neither the FULL_REFUND uplift nor the driver-conduct referral can issue on this record.

No POL-RD-10 escalation trigger fires. trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown all carry trip TRP-00525 with consistent timestamps; the trace is unimpaired under POL-RD-07; no exculpatory clause is invoked against a missing artifact; the disputed sum is far below the SGD 150.00 ceiling; and every charge line has a counterpart in the trace or the trip record. The case is ruleable on the papers.

No deciding artifact is impaired. trip_record, gps_trace, fare_breakdown and both party profiles all carry weight_multiplier 1.0; only the absent advisory sits at 0.0, and it carries no deciding fact. The POL-GEN-02(2) confidence cap therefore never drops below the 0.70 platform floor, so no POL-RD-10(1) escalation can be founded on the bundle.

No traffic advisory covers this corridor. EV-ADVIS-00525-01 is MISSING, carries weight_multiplier 0.0 and issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, and can carry no fact; its absence is itself citable. The record therefore discloses no road closure or traffic event of any kind, and the driver's case does not rest on one - POL-RD-01 shows there is no deviation to excuse.

Nothing in the record ties the fare difference to the route. The in-app chat log for this trip is empty (0 messages), so no rider instruction and no in-trip complaint is recorded, and POL-RD-04 is unavailable on this record; the trace independently shows the route was not deviated. The route-deviation theory on which this claim is filed has nothing to stand on.

ruling.explanation:
To both parties: this is really two questions, and they come out differently.

THE ROUTE. There was no deviation. The governing trace figure (EV-GPS-00525, trace_distance_km 4.58) against the booked optimal of 4.4 km (EV-TRIP-00525) is an excess of 0.18 km, or 4.09 per cent. POL-RD-01 requires both gates to be passed — more than 0.8 km absolute AND more than 20 per cent of optimal — and neither is. So the driver is right that nothing route-related is refundable, the POL-RD-02 recomputation does not run, and the POL-RD-06 uplift and driver-conduct referral cannot issue (driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against 250 completed trips over 90 days, so no pattern exists). The trace is also clean for POL-RD-07 purposes — 85 fixes, 10-second cadence, 100 per cent coverage, no gaps — so no corroboration requirement and no POL-RD-10(3) escalation arise. I accept the driver's claims on POL-RD-01, POL-RD-07, POL-RD-08 (as to the route), POL-RD-09 (no ERP, toll or surcharge defect) and POL-RD-06.

THE MONEY. The fare is a different matter, and it does not depend on a deviation. EV-FARE-00525 shows an UPFRONT_QUOTE trip: quoted_fare_sgd 13.00, total_charged 17.50. POL-RD-11 governs such a fare, so the rider gets no distance-or-time refund — but limb (a) gives her the amount by which the charge exceeds the quote plus only the pass-through and statutory lines (ERP and tolls actually crossed, a properly chargeable airport surcharge, waiting_time_fee). Those lines are all 0.00 here, and there is no gantry and no airport surcharge, so nothing legitimately sits on top of the 13.00 quote to explain the difference. 17.50 − 13.00 = 4.50, and that 4.50 is refunded in full. The 13.00 quote stands because the ride was taken. This is a PARTIAL_REFUND: part of the 17.50 contested is returned, not all of it, so I do not read the claim as reaching the whole charged amount.

The driver does not defend the figure — his own statement on file concedes he keyed in another passenger's amount — and that concession is consistent with the arithmetic. Because the ride was performed and the quote covers it, the refund is the 4.50 excess and not the full 17.50. I accept the rider's POL-RD-11, POL-RD-09/POL-RD-11 and POL-GEN-03 claims, which are the basis of this award; her POL-RD-01 point that no deviation exists is correct and is why the route ground adds nothing to her refund.

PROFILE AND CONDUCT. No profile field decides anything. The rider correctly argues that her own counters (deviation_claims_60d and deviation_claims_60d_substantiated, both 0) do not engage the POL-RD-08 corroboration rule, and that the driver's prior_deviation_flags is a lifetime counter that POL-GEN-01 makes context only — the flag on that claim is a context-only mention only, not a ground of decision, and it changes nothing. The rider's remark that this is the 'fourth time' is noted as an open question for the platform; no clause turns it into a referral, because POL-RD-06 needs a trailing-90-day pattern that is not present, and the general statement of the overcharge is remedied by the refund itself.

CONFIDENCE AND REFERRALS. The deciding fact — that the charge exceeds the quote — is carried by EV-FARE-00525, weight_multiplier 1.0, so the POL-GEN-02(2) cap is 1.0. The absent traffic advisory (EV-ADVIS-00525-01, weight 0.0, MISSING_ARTIFACT) carries no deciding fact, and no exculpatory clause invokes it. No POL-RD-10 escalation trigger fires and no clause produces a referral: there is no unmatched gantry or wrongly applied airport surcharge for POL-RD-09(4), and no POL-RD-06(c) conduct referral.

To both parties. The fare was an upfront-quoted fare, and that is what decides the money here. The fare ledger (EV-FARE-00525) shows a quoted fare of SGD 13.00 and a total charged of SGD 17.50 — SGD 4.50 more than the price fixed at booking. POL-RD-11 governs upfront-quoted trips: because the rider's distance and time were fixed when she booked, no distance-or-time refund runs (POL-RD-02 is switched off), but any amount by which the charged total exceeds the quote — plus only any properly chargeable ERP, toll, airport surcharge or waiting-time fee — is refunded in full. Those extra lines are all zero on this ledger (ERP 0.00, airport surcharge 0.00, waiting-time fee 0.00), so the whole SGD 4.50 excess over the SGD 13.00 quote comes back to the rider. The SGD 13.00 quote itself stands, because the ride was taken. The result is a PARTIAL_REFUND of SGD 4.50 out of the SGD 17.50 charged. To the driver: your statement on file — that you keyed in another passenger's amount by mistake — is the counterparty statement in this case. It confirms that SGD 17.50 does not price this 4.6 km, 14-minute trip from Bedok Mall to Parkway Parade. It carries no weight multiplier and neither adds to nor subtracts from the ledger figure, with which it is consistent. On the route-deviation theory: no deviation is established. The governing trace (EV-GPS-00525) is 4.58 km against a 4.4 km optimal, an excess of 0.18 km (4.09%), below both POL-RD-01 gates of 0.8 km and 20%. The driver's advocate is right about that, and about POL-RD-06 (no repeat pattern: 0 flags against 250 completed trips) and POL-RD-07 (the trace is unimpaired: 85 fixes, 10-second interval, no gaps, max gap 0 s). But a deviation is not what this refund rests on: POL-RD-11(a) is a billing remedy and is available whether or not a route deviation exists, exactly as POL-RD-09(4) is. The rider's initial-burden argument under POL-RD-08 goes to proving a deviation and does not touch the over-quote difference, and no billing-integrity defect under POL-RD-09(4) exists (no gantry or surcharge line at all), so that limb neither adds nor subtracts. No escalation trigger under POL-RD-10 fires: the trip record, trace and ledger all carry trip TRP-00525 with consistent timestamps, the trace is unimpaired, no exculpatory clause is invoked against a missing artifact, every charge line has a counterpart in the trace or trip record, and the sum is far below the SGD 150.00 ceiling. Under POL-GEN-02 no deciding artifact sits below weight 1.0 — the only artifact at 0.0 is the missing traffic advisory (EV-ADVIS-00525-01), which carries no fact — so the confidence cap is 1.0. On the profile material: driver_profile.prior_deviation_flags is a lifetime counter and is context only under POL-GEN-01; it plays no part in this decision. No clause produces a referral on this record: there is no material deviation for POL-RD-06(c) and no unmatched or wrongly applied charge line for POL-RD-09(4).
